_comment: Lancaster — nine-stage-generation workbook. IMPORTED AND PUBLISHED 2026-07-31 (5 of 9), then 7 of 9 on 2026-08-05 when ADR-16 released the two rows held only on a low-precision coordinate. The 'NOT YET IMPORTED' claim that stood here until 2026-08-05 was stale from the day the batch landed. This metro also carries a SECOND batch — scripts/metros/lancaster-v3.json, 27 rows, same metro_area — and the two are independent: this config's stages must never be run with the intent of touching v3's rows, and vice versa. envelope is NOW SET (derived 2026-07-31 from the MSA county list, not from the observed bbox) — see _envelope_comment for the counties used, the derivation rule and the containment cross-check. workbook.aliases: this workbook labels the venue's own source URL `name_source_url` rather than `website`/`source_url`; that is a pure synonym rename, scoped here rather than added to the global table.
_envelope_comment: Derived from the Lancaster, PA MSA COUNTY LIST, not from the observed venue bounding box. The observed bbox is only a LOWER bound — it says where the venues we happened to find are, not where the metro is, so an envelope cut to it would reject a legitimate future venue near the metro edge. Envelope = the union of the OSM boundary-polygon bounding boxes for the 1 MSA county (Lancaster)), rounded OUTWARD to 0.01 deg. Cross-check: contains all 6 geocoded venue(s) of 9 in this batch (observed lat 40.0148..40.1569, lng -76.4203..-76.3021).
_expected_publish_comment: AUTHORED 2026-08-05 FROM THE PROJECTION, NOT FROM A GUESS — the same sequence lancaster-v3 used. This batch ran its whole 2026-07-31 import with no expected_publish block at all, so its split was never machine-checked; `--stage=project` printed 'no expected_publish block ... split not machine-checked' on every run. The block was written only after reading the 7/9 projection this config's own --stage=project produced, and it is asserted at BOTH project (from the artifact) and publish (recomputed from the database). count 7 = the 5 published 2026-07-31 plus hempfield-reccenter and lititz-reccenter, which were held solely on a low-precision coordinate and which ADR-16 releases behind an approximate-location label. Both hold reasons are 'no coordinate' — the one condition ADR-16 deliberately did NOT relax, because a label can qualify a pin, it cannot invent one. THE REASON STRINGS ARE 'no coordinate' AND NOT THE FULLER PUBLISH-STAGE STRING ON PURPOSE: assertExpectedPublish matches with includes(), and the overlook row now computes 'no coordinate' at project (the artifact still records research_status=verified) but 'no coordinate; research_status=held' at publish (the candidate was retired to 'held' on 2026-08-05). 'no coordinate' is the substring true at both stages. If a hold ever clears, move the row out of this block deliberately; never edit the block to match an output.
